types.examples: Shock, low oxygen, anaphylaxis, low sugar, K 6.5+, NEWS2 7+
Identity doubt, unknown allergy, invalid consent, unknown pregnancy status, unacknowledged critical result, incomplete checklist

types.effect: Must be done within a clock
types.examples: Sepsis antibiotics, analgesia, fluids for dehydration
Ectopic, cholangitis, perforation, duct stone, new AF, MI

types.effect: S1 usually deferred after review/re-time; S2 correct in parallel
types.examples: BP 180/110+, HbA1c above 69, anaemia, salts, anticoagulant timing, fasting

ladder.question: Is anything immediately life-threatening? (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, low sugar, anaphylaxis, NEWS2 7+)
ladder.action: Fix that FIRST using ABCDE and call for help — everything else waits

ladder.question: Is there a hard safety blocker? (identity doubt, allergy unknown before a drug, consent invalid, positive pregnancy test with pain)
ladder.action: Resolve before any non-emergency treatment or transfer

ladder.question: Is there a time-critical treatment? (antibiotics within 1 h in sepsis, pain relief, fluids for shock, potassium 6.5+)
ladder.action: Do it now — in parallel with the remaining work

ladder.question: Does any finding change the diagnosis or pathway? (ectopic, cholangitis, burst appendix, duct stone)
Do treatments conflict? (e.g. fluids vs heart failure; best antibiotic vs allergy; painkiller vs kidneys)
ladder.action: Choose the safest alternative (table 14B.3); ask senior/anaesthetist

ladder.question: Is it S1 with any fixable problem left?
ladder.action: Senior/anaesthetic review → usually optimise first (defer / re-time / rebook)

ladder.question: Prepare, consent, hand over
ladder.action: listing EVERY problem and its plan in the SBAR

priorities.meaning: immediate threat to airway, breathing or circulation (or brain: glucose)
